This fear stems from seeing that car hanging halfway off the bridge in the fog, even though I logically know it's not realistic and everyone else drives over them just fine.\n\nDoctor: Do you fear heights in general, such as standing on a balcony, looking down from a tall building, or using a ladder, or is the fear only when driving or riding over bridges and high roads?\n\nPatient: No, I don't fear heights in general at all. The fear is strictly focused on bridges, overpasses, and elevated or narrow stretches of road where there is a drop-off. It's really the combination of the height and that specific, terrifying thought of sliding off the edge of an elevated structure.\n\nDoctor: Do you fear heights in general, like standing on a balcony or looking out from a tall building, or is the fear only when driving or riding over bridges and elevated roads?\n\nPatient: No, I don't have a general fear of heights like being on a balcony or inside a tall building. The fear is strictly tied to driving or riding over bridges and elevated, narrow roadways. My intense fear, pounding heart, and sweaty hands are specifically triggered when I have to drive over bridges, see pictures of them, or realize a route is taking me toward an overpass. It is very specifically tied to those elevated roadways.\n\nDoctor: When you are on or approaching those bridges or high roads, do you worry mainly about something bad happening there, like falling or losing control, rather than being judged by other people or having a panic attack?\n\nPatient: Yes, exactly. I get this huge, sick fear that my car is just going to slide right off the edge, even though I know in my head that's not realistic and everyone else drives over them just fine. It's not about being judged by others at all—it's just that terrifying feeling of going over the side.\n\nDoctor: Do you also have this intense fear in other situations involving heights, such as looking down from tall buildings, standing on balconies, or using ladders?\n\nPatient: No, I don't think I have that same fear with things like balconies or ladders. It really seems to be limited to just driving on those bridges and high stretches of road.\n\nDoctor: Do you have this same intense fear in other situations involving heights, such as standing on a balcony, looking down from a tall building, or using a ladder?\n\nPatient: No, I don't really experience that kind of intense fear with balconies, tall buildings, or ladders. The fear is very specifically tied to driving over bridges, overpasses, or those high stretches of road.\n\nDoctor: When you are afraid on those bridges or high roads, is the fear mainly about the height itself, or is it more about being in a situation where you might be trapped or unable to escape?\n\nPatient: It's not about being trapped at all. It's really just this overwhelming fear that my car is going to slide right off the edge of the road, just like the car I saw hanging off the guardrail in that bad accident.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a similar intense fear in other situations where there is no height involved, such as seeing a car accident, being in traffic, or thinking about bridges because of a past traumatic event?\n\nPatient: No, I don't get that intense fear in normal traffic or other situations where there is no height involved. It really is strictly tied to those high, narrow bridges and overpasses where I feel like my car could slide off. Normal driving or seeing an accident on a flat road doesn't trigger this overwhelming panic at all.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel this same fear in other situations involving heights, like standing on a balcony, looking down from a tall building, or using a ladder? Or is it only when driving on bridges or high roads?\n\nPatient: No, it is strictly when I am driving on those bridges and high roads. I don't feel this way at all on balconies, in tall buildings, or on ladders. It's really just the specific fear of my car sliding off those elevated roadways.\n\nDoctor: Do you also feel this fear in other situations where you are being driven or traveling, such as in a car, bus, train, or airplane, or is it only when you are driving on bridges and high roads?\n\nPatient: No, I don't fear general travel like trains or airplanes at all. It is strictly tied to bridges and high roads, even if my husband is the one driving me. The fear is strictly focused on bridges, overpasses, and elevated or narrow stretches of road where there is a drop-off.
